message.content:
Here’s a quick snapshot of some of the most celebrated American composers across different eras:

| Composer | Era / Style | Notable Works |
|----------|-------------|---------------|
| **John Philip Sousa** (1854‑1932) | Romantic/Patriotic marches | “Stars and Stripes Forever,” “The Washington Post” |
| **George Gershwin** (1898‑1937) | Jazz‑influenced classical | “Rhapsody in Blue,” “An American in Paris” |
| **Aaron Copland** (1900‑1990) | Mid‑20th‑century modernism | “Appalachian Spring,” “Fanfare for the Common Man” |
| **Leonard Bernstein** (1918‑1990) | Broadway & symphonic | “West Side Story,” “Candide” |
| **Samuel Barber** (1910‑1981) | Neoclassical/Modern | “Adagio for Strings,” “Knoxville: Summer of 1915” |
| **Philip Glass** (born 1937) | Minimalist | “Einstein on the Beach,” “Glassworks” |
| **John Adams** (born 1947) | Contemporary minimalism | “Short Ride in a Fast Machine,” “Nixon in China” |
| **Steve Reich** (born 1936) | Minimalist | “Music for 18 Musicians,” “Different Trains” |
| **William Grant Still** (1895‑1978) | African‑American classical | “Afro-American Symphony,” “Bluebird” |
| **Charles Ives** (1874‑1954) | Experimental | “The Unanswered Question,” “Concord Sonata” |

These figures have shaped American music from patriotic marches to avant‑garde minimalism, leaving a lasting legacy on both national and global stages.
